parts.given_text: A 10 kg block slides down a 30° incline after its string is cut. Its acceleration down the incline is 2.4 m s⁻² (rounded). It starts from rest; find the time to travel 4.0 m.

sup-73347e8dc6144c72-w9:a.hint: Draw a force equation for each connected body, using compatible positive directions along the string.
notes: An inextensible taut string links the accelerations. A light string over an ideal pulley has the same tension on both sides.
To find acceleration, combine the equations to eliminate internal tension. Then substitute back into a single-body equation to find the tension.

sup-73347e8dc6144c72-w9:b.i.hint: Compare the upward resistive force with the weight at each stage, rather than assuming the acceleration stays constant.
notes: Use resultant force = ma with a declared positive direction. Drag increases with speed in the stated model, while weight is essentially constant.
Terminal speed means balanced forces and zero acceleration; it does not mean zero speed. Opening a parachute can reverse the direction of acceleration before the motion reverses.

notes: Use E_k = ½mv² and near-surface ΔE_p = mgΔh. Work by a constant force is W = Fs cos θ, using the angle between force and displacement.
The work–energy theorem uses the net work. With friction, include the energy dissipated rather than assuming mechanical energy is conserved.
